review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its uses. I looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning and found two cases. First, shift_infinite and right_target_left_finite repeat the same "range k ∪ shifted image" covering argument. Second, left_injective and right_injective are mirror-image proofs, and both call the symmetric anchor_mem_* lemmas. I left out the three one-line card_*_le proofs, because they are short and thin. I did not check the proposed rewrites with Lean. The `Equiv.sumComm` / `Set.preimage_injective` names and the exact simp behaviour should be confirmed when the change is made. I also did not search the other users of these lemmas beyond the grep; no signature change is proposed.

findings.problem: Both proofs show that a set of naturals is finite from the finiteness of its k-shift, by the same argument. They cover the set by `Finset.range k ∪ (k + ·) '' _`, split on `n < k`, and rebuild the preimage element `n - k` with `Nat.add_sub_of_le`. shift_infinite is the contrapositive of this fact for a general C. right_target_left_finite redoes the argument for C = {n | inl n ∈ rightTarget j E}. It does so instead of using `tail_mem_right`, which already says the shifted set is E. The case split and the `n - k` reconstruction are written out twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma before shift_infinite: `theorem finite_of_shift_finite {C : Set ℕ} (k : ℕ) (hf : {n | k + n ∈ C}.Finite) : C.Finite`. Its proof is the current body of lines 157–162: cover C by `range k ∪ (k + ·) '' {n | k + n ∈ C}`, split on `n < k`, and use the witness `n - k`. Then `shift_infinite hC k := fun hf => hC (finite_of_shift_finite k hf)`. And `right_target_left_finite j hE := finite_of_shift_finite k (hE.subset fun n hn => (tail_mem_right j E n).mp hn)`. The hypotheses are unchanged. The membership `n ∈ {n | k + n ∈ {m | Sum.inl m ∈ rightTarget j E}}` is defeq to `Sum.inl (k+n) ∈ rightTarget j E`, which is the left side of `tail_mem_right`.
findings.benefit: The tail-shift covering argument is proved once. right_target_left_finite becomes a one-line corollary that uses the already stated `tail_mem_right` instead of redoing the `if n < k` analysis. A later change to the arithmetic only needs to be made in one place.

findings.problem: The two injectivity proofs are the same argument with `Sum.inl` and `Sum.inr` swapped. Each separates the anchor index through the missing anchor, substitutes, then separates the tail through the point `k + n`. The 15-line blocks differ only in the side constructor. The two definitions are mirror images, since `rightTarget j E` is `leftTarget j E` pulled back along `Sum.swap`. The file never states this, so every symmetric fact needs a second proof (the anchor_mem_*, tail_mem_* and *_injective pairs).
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem rightTarget_eq_preimage_swap {k} (j : Fin k) (E : Set ℕ) : rightTarget j E = Sum.swap ⁻¹' leftTarget j E := by ext (n | n) <;> rfl`. Check the defeq first, because `Sum.swap` reduces on constructors and the `Sum.elim` branches should line up. Then derive right_injective from left_injective. Given `he : rightTarget i D = rightTarget j E`, rewrite with the lemma on both sides. Then apply `Set.preimage_injective.mpr Equiv.sumComm.surjective` to get `leftTarget i D = leftTarget j E`, and finish with `left_injective`. The proof then no longer repeats the anchor/tail separation argument. The same lemma could also shorten `left_ne_right`.
findings.benefit: The only genuinely hard injectivity argument is stated once, and right_injective becomes a short symmetry corollary. The left/right relationship is recorded explicitly, so later lemmas can be derived from one side instead of copy-pasted.
